title: In a high-dimensional product graph, two isolated vertices of the random subgraph are typically at distance at least three

standard_prerequisites.name: The parameters of the model: n the order and d the dimension-regularity parameter of the product graph, p the edge probability, and the constant alpha_M controlling the one-edge overlap factor
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at source lines 494-508; the model and the relation d = Theta_M(log n) are set up earlier in the paper (around source lines 201-240)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the two counts of ordered pairs (nd adjacent pairs and nd squared pairs at distance two) and the constant alpha_M in the bound (1-p)^(2d-1) <= alpha_M (1-p)^(2d).

core_obligations: Count the pairs to which the union bound is applied: at most nd ordered adjacent pairs and at most nd^2 ordered pairs at distance two (proof line 494).
Compute the isolation probability for non-adjacent u and v: the incident edge sets are disjoint, so the probability that both are isolated is (1-p)^(2d) (proof lines 495-498).
Handle the adjacent case: the incident edge sets overlap in exactly one edge, so the probability is (1-p)^(2d-1), which is at most alpha_M (1-p)^(2d) for some constant alpha_M (proof lines 499-503).

Bound the expected number of ordered pairs of isolated vertices at distance at most two by alpha_M nd^2 (1-p)^(2d), and use the range satisfied by p to turn it into alpha_M d^(2+1/25)/n = o(1) (proof lines 504-508).
Conclude with Markov's inequality that with high probability there is no such pair, which is the assertion of the lemma (proof lines 509-510).
proof_roadmap: 分类讨论：不相邻的点对孤立概率为 (1-p)^{2d}，相邻的点对为 (1-p)^{2d-1}，后者用常数 alpha_M 吸收。
用 p 的取值范围把期望压到 o(1)，再由 Markov 不等式得到 whp 结论。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the geometric separation lemma for isolated vertices in the random subgraph of a high-dimensional product graph (author lemma at source lines 489-491, label lem:isolates-far). Its proof (source lines 493-510) is a second-moment count whose content is the case distinction on the pair: for non-adjacent u and v the incident edge sets are disjoint and the isolation probability is (1-p)^(2d), while for adjacent pairs the sets overlap in exactly one edge, which changes the exponent to 2d-1 and has to be absorbed by a constant alpha_M before the union bound can be applied (proof lines 495-503). The counting step then uses the author's range for p, displayed as eq:mu-range and delivered as a context span, to convert alpha_M nd^2 (1-p)^(2d) into alpha_M d^(2+1/25)/n = o(1) (proof lines 504-508). The closing appeal is Markov's inequality. H2.
